newsitem.title: INDIA: Miss World media accused of racial discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Miss World media accused of racial discrimination.

text.p: As if suicide protests were not enough controversy already for the Miss World beauty pageant in India, African contestants have accused media covering the event of racial discrimination.
Organisers have already tightened security after a suicide protest against the pageant, a threat of more to come, and a pending court ruling on whether to ban the show.
Now the African contingent among the 88 competitors say the media is shunning them because they are black.

"I didn't expect this kind of discrimination in India. I am really disappointed," Shose Akaro of Tanzania told Reuters as contestants mingled among the press at a dinner on Saturday night at the Bangalore hotel where the women are staying.
"The Indian press has totally ignored us (black Africans) from the day we have landed in your country. Just about everyone in the press is paying attention only to the whites," she said.
Miss Zambia, Alice Banda, felt similarly ignored.
"We have no problem with the (other) contestants or the organisers or the hotel staff or the organisers. It is only discrimination by the press that hits you," Banda, a law student, said.
"Just look at them. They are going after the whites." she said as a battery of television crews and photographers, both Indian and foreign, pursued white contestants.
"How can there be a fair judgement if the focus is only on them," Akara said.
Many of the contestants from Africa have complained to the publicity agency handling the event.
"They genuinely feel they are being ignored," said Ashwani Singhla, a spokesman for Clea Public relations.
Akaro said it was apparent that some members of the press thought the African contestants were ignorant.

"Let me illustrate. You know after asking a Western contestant for her views on World Bank aid to developing countries, one of the press guys turned to us and asked whether the weather in our country was similar to India and those kind of questions."
